source.title: Not Every Token Needs Forgetting: Selective Unlearning to Limit Change in Utility in Large Language Model Unlearning
source.authors: Yixin Wan; Anil Ramakrishna; Kai-Wei Chang; Volkan Cevher; Rahul Gupta

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Table 2 is flattened in a way that does not reliably associate all its values with individual methods and metrics.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates whether unlearning reduces performance on targeted data while preserving utility, but it does not test recovery attacks.
record.gate_note: The paper tests forgetting and retained utility, not whether fine-tuning, internal edits, quantization, or prompting recover the forgotten information. Table 2 reports relevant outcomes, but its flattened text does not reliably support method-to-metric value assignments; those cells are omitted rather than guessed. The paper's explicit qualitative results and the clearly assigned MMLU results are recorded.
record.test_reason: This is a methods paper proposing Selective Unlearning (SU). It reports only forget and utility scores for SU against six baselines on TOFU and MUSE-News. It runs no recovery attack (fine-tuning, ablation, quantization or prompting), so it never tests whether unlearning is shallow or robust. Its forget and utility numbers are its own method's performance, not a test of version A's robustness clause or of any other version.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right. The authors conclude SU forgets effectively while preserving retain utility better than baselines. Their own Table 2, however, shows SU's MUSE KnowMem (Retain) (0.20/0.19) below GA+KL, NPO+KL and NPO+GD. SU's MUSE MMLU (0.19/0.26) is at or below chance, so the utility-preservation claim holds mainly for TOFU truth ratios.
record.recipe_differences: The study proposes selective token-level gradient ascent, using assistant models to select tokens, and applies gradient descent on retain data. It does not test the recovery-attack recipe in the claim.
record.method_sensitivity: Selection threshold affects retained performance; the paper reports a larger influence on MUSE-News than TOFU. It selects different thresholds and assistant-model data splits for different benchmark and assistant settings.

fits_no_version.finding: On the MUSE model, every unlearned model, including SU, scores at or below chance on MMLU (GA 0.000, GD 0.21, SU-LLM 0.19, SU-N-Gram 0.26). No original-model MMLU is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient-ascent-based unlearning, even when token-selective, can collapse general ability to chance on MMLU.

record.problems: No recovery attacks are tested. The authors state that experiments were not extended to larger scales or bigger LLMs. Table 2's flattened text prevents reliable assignment of its numerical values to methods and metrics.
record.rows_left_out: Numerical cells from Table 2 are omitted because the provided flattened layout does not reliably associate the values with individual methods and metrics. The paper's explicit qualitative outcomes from that table are recorded in r1–r8.

untested.parts: Whether simple attacks recover the knowledge. Forget/utility scores are reported only as own-method benchmarking.
All parts; SU is not claimed or tested to resist recovery attacks

record.verdict_notes: Table 2 can be read column-wise. Baselines are listed in order GA, GA+GD, GA+KL, NPO, NPO+KL, NPO+GD, and the SU rows are cleanly laid out. The record's claim that the values cannot be assigned is overstated. The original-model row in Table 2 has 8 values for 7 metric columns, so its alignment is uncertain. No recovery attacks are run anywhere in the paper. The record's T2/tests guess and its 'supports A' label are not justified.

versions.untested_parts: Whether simple attacks recover targeted knowledge after unlearning.
Recovery by fine-tuning on small, unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten-fact examples.
Recovery by ablating an activation direction or evidence that unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
Recovery by rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
A method's resistance to the recovery attacks listed in the claim.

rows.subject: MUSE-News model (checkpoint name not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate forget performance after Selective Unlearning with N-Gram assistant models.
rows.measure: Forgetting on the MUSE-News forget split
rows.value: The authors report effective forgetting and comparable forget performance to existing methods.
rows.note: Table 2 has numerical results, but flattened text does not reliably associate its values with this method and measure.
rows.check: Own-method performance with no attack. The value is readable from Table 2: SU (N-Gram) VerbMem 0.02 and KnowMem (Forget) 0.01.

rows.subject: MUSE-News model (checkpoint name not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Evaluate retained-set utility after Selective Unlearning with N-Gram assistant models.
rows.measure: Knowledge memorization on the retain set
rows.value: The authors report better retained-set knowledge memorization than baseline unlearning approaches.
rows.note: The paper states that both SU methods improve MUSE-News retain utility.
rows.check: Own-method comparison. Table 2 gives SU (N-Gram) KnowMem (Retain) 0.20, below GA+KL 0.26, NPO+KL 0.25 and NPO+GD 0.30, and far below the original's apparent 0.55–0.64. The row's 'better than baselines' value is not borne out.
